changes.subject: win32: `hashDoc` / `sourceDoc` spell workspace-relative docs POSIX-style on every platform
changes.why: MEASURED DEFECT, pre-existing and red on the Windows baseline: `packages/mpd-verify-plugin/test/row.test.ts` AC-D2 failed on a PRISTINE tree (evidence below). `ledger.ts#hashDoc` relativized with `path.startsWith(workspace + "/")` — a POSIX-shaped test — so on win32, where both sides carry `\`, the prefix never matched and a document INSIDE the workspace was stored with its absolute, machine-specific path. `tools.ts#sourceDoc` carried the same class of assumption in `path.startsWith("/")`. The record's `basis.frozenContract.path` is workspace-relative POSIX, so on win32 the two halves of ONE record disagreed.

Every other text file — `*.js` above all, i.e. every `packages/*/dist/*.js` — therefore landed on disk with CRLF, while the BLOB and a fresh `bun build` are both LF. Three byte-reading subjects answered red with nothing wrong in the tree: `verify-dist-fresh` reported 31 of 31 targets stale, `verify-vendor` reported `sha256 mismatch` for two fingerprint-pinned `.js` assets, and the per-package `F1 shipped artifact` arms reddened. issue1SidebarDiagnosis.status: NOT a plugin code defect. Diagnosed with evidence; the runtime repair is an INSTALL action outside this repository (stated below).
issue1SidebarDiagnosis.guardDecision: The shipped mount guard logged `[mpd-better-sidebar] mount guard: DISABLED - dsh-better-sidebar is resolvable from neither the profile node_modules nor the bundle` in .mpd/logs/mpd-patch-guards.log, and evaluating the SHIPPED `!!js` expression against the real profiles reproduces it: web -> DISABLED=false (ENABLED) after the checkout was installed; desktop -> DISABLED=true.
measuredFacts: The GUI on 127.0.0.1:19387 is `DeepSeek Harness.exe` running the `desktop` profile (C:\Users\zhao.yinan\.dsh\profiles\desktop). `scripts/dump-config.ts --profile desktop` refuses: `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`.

This checkout had NO node_modules at all: `dsh-better-sidebar` is a devDependency + optional peer, so the bundle's own copy was absent. `bun install` materialized it (441 packages, dsh-better-sidebar@0.24.1), and the `web` profile's guard then answers ENABLED.

The `desktop` profile's <profile>/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd is a JUNCTION whose target is `C:\MyDoc\my-power-dsh` - a path that does NOT exist (the checkout is `C:\MyDoc\DshProj\My-Power-Dsh`). Its plugin-manager log records the stale link verbatim: `@mpd-dsh/mpd link:C:/MyDoc/my-power-dsh`.

`dsh-better-sidebar` exists NOWHERE in the desktop profile, and no profile declares `@mpd-dsh/mpd` in `dsh.profile.bundles`. `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` - the aggregate the desktop profile DOES carry - does not depend on the sidebar host either.
issue1SidebarDiagnosis.designBoundRecordedNotChanged: `npm pack --dry-run` lists 944 files and ZERO node_modules entries, so the DOCUMENTED one-command install ships no sidebar host; and because the host is a devDependency + optional peer it is not installed as a dependency, so clause 1 of the mount guard disables the row there too. AGENTS.md §8 records this as DELIBERATE (pnpm 11 hard-exits on node-pty's postinstall and `dsh plugin add` has no approval channel), so this wave did NOT change the dependency declaration - that is a captain/user decision, and it cannot be verified here without a real install.
repairForTheUserMachine: The checkout now has node_modules (this wave ran `bun install`), so the `web` profile is repaired by that alone.

For the running `desktop` profile: re-install the bundle from the CURRENT checkout path so the junction points at it, e.g. `dsh plugin --profile desktop add C:\MyDoc\DshProj\My-Power-Dsh`, then restart the app. The stale `C:\MyDoc\my-power-dsh` target cannot resolve anywhere.

reviewFollowUp.source: CodeRabbit review on PR #38, packages/mpd-verify-plugin/src/ledger.ts (Data Integrity, Minor).
reviewFollowUp.finding: The win32 containment repair normalized BOTH sides with `.replace(/\\/g, "/")`, which is LOSSY on POSIX: a backslash is a legal FILENAME character there, so a document named `a\b.md` was stored as `a/b.md` — a path that no longer identifies the file that was hashed.
reviewFollowUp.verdict: VALID, and it is a defect this wave INTRODUCED. Fixed rather than waived.
fix: containment now uses the platform's own `relative(workspace, path)` plus `isAbsolute` (no prefix guessing at all), which also makes the comparison CASE-INSENSITIVE on win32 and collapses `.`/`..` the way the OS does
the separator translation moved into `toPosixRelative(rel, separator = sep)` and happens ONLY where a backslash is a separator
reviewFollowUp.whyTheSeparatorIsAParameter: The invariant to falsify is "a POSIX filename may contain a backslash and keeps it". On win32 that filename cannot exist, so an arm written against the FILESYSTEM could only be skipped on the platform most development happens on — and a skipped arm proves nothing. Taking the separator as an argument makes both branches executable everywhere. (The CI `gates` job runs NO unit tests, so a skipped arm would not have been exercised by CI either.)
arms: packages/mpd-verify-plugin/test/law.test.ts: a hashDoc arm asserts a document INSIDE the workspace is stored workspace-relative POSIX while one OUTSIDE keeps the caller's spelling (both halves, so the arm cannot pass by always answering a relative path)

packages/mpd-verify-plugin/test/law.test.ts: a toPosixRelative arm asserts `/` keeps a backslash in the filename while `\` translates it, plus the nested/root/idempotent shapes and the platform default
